property_summary: For any immutable-args calldata, C.owner() must return the address packed at arg offset 0x0 (the owner), never the one at 0x14 (the collateral); the mutant reads 0x14 so it returns the collateral address instead.

For any call, C.owner() must return the address embedded at immutable-arg offset 0x0 (bytes 10..29 of the appended word); the mutant instead returns the word at offset 0x3c (zero for short calldata), so owner() != the embedded address for any nonzero fuzzed address.

For any address whose low 16 bits equal 0x22 (so the immutable-args offset resolves to 0), a calldata call owner(selector ++ a) must return exactly a; the mutant reads offset 0x3c instead of 0x0, which lies past the 36-byte calldata, so it returns address(0) and breaks the rule.

For any clone-style calldata whose trailing two bytes encode a valid immutable-args offset, C.owner() must return the 20-byte address embedded at immutable-arg offset 0x0; the mutant reads offset 0x3c (past the calldata, yielding zero) and so returns the wrong address for any nonzero embedded address.

For any calldata carrying immutable args, C.owner() must return the address stored at args offset 0x0 (the owner); the mutant reads offset 0x28 and returns a different address whenever the two 32-byte arg words differ.

property_summary: In any cooler, the immutable collateral token address stored at offset 0x14 differs from the immutable owner address stored at offset 0x0, so c.collateral() != c.owner() for every admissible (owner, collateral) pair; the mutant reads offset 0x0 in collateral(), making collateral() return the owner address and violating the inequality whenever owner != collateral.

For any actor generating a cooler through CoolerFactory with a given collateral token address distinct from the actor, the cooler's public collateral() getter must return exactly that collateral token address; the mutant reads immutable arg offset 0x0 instead of 0x14, so collateral() returns the owner and violates this equality.

In any properly-instantiated cooler whose immutable args are (owner at 0x0, collateral at 0x14, debt at 0x28, factory at 0x3c), the public collateral() getter must return exactly the collateral token address stored at offset 0x14; the mutant reads offset 0x0 instead, so it returns the owner address and the equality fails whenever owner != collateral.

For any factory-generated cooler with distinct collateral and debt token addresses, C.collateral() must return the collateral token passed to generateCooler (immutable arg at 0x14); the mutant reads offset 0x28 and instead returns the debt token, breaking the rule whenever the two differ.

For any two distinct token addresses embedded as immutable args, c.collateral() must return the address stored at immutable-arg offset 0x14; the mutant reads offset 0x28 and returns the other (debt) token, breaking the rule whenever the two differ.

For any calldata of the clone form (selector + immutable args with a 2-byte length suffix), C.collateral() returns the 20 bytes at immutable-arg offset 0x14 (the collateral token), while the mutant returns the 20 bytes at offset 0x28 (the debt token), so whenever the two embedded addresses differ the mutant's return differs from the reference's.

For any owner/collateral/debt triple, a Cooler created by the factory must report collateral() equal to the collateral token address supplied at creation (immutable arg at offset 0x14); the mutant reads offset 0x3c and so reports the factory address instead, breaking this for (almost) all inputs.

For any factory-created Cooler, collateral() must return the collateral token address baked into the immutable args, which is always distinct from the factory address; the mutant reads offset 0x3c and returns the factory address, making collateral() equal factory() and violating the rule.
